This instantiation is a 1x1-output / N=1 case where OH, OW, N and both weight vectors folded to scalars, i.e. the store degenerated into a uniform-address store of a rank-2 value. The failure is therefore tied to the degenerate rank-2 broadcast-store form, not to fp16 stores in general.

record.hypothesis: The generic kernel's rank-2 tile store, which in degenerate shapes (OH==OW==1, N==1) collapses to a splat pointer plus a rank-2 value, is what the Ascend ConvertTritonIRToLinalgIR lowering rejects. Emitting only rank-1 tiles whose store pointer is built from a per-lane offset tensor (the form the native IR uses) removes that rejected form while keeping the same arithmetic and clamping semantics, so all formal cases compile and pass.
record.change: Compatibility/structure change in the generic path only (no 2x-path edit): replace the rank-2 (BLOCK_Y x BLOCK_X) tiled generic kernel with a flat 1-D kernel over the output plane. One program handles BLOCK contiguous output pixels of one (n,c) plane; idx = pid*BLOCK + arange, oh = idx // OW, ow = idx % OW, the same real_h/real_w -> h0/w0/h1/w1 clamping and weight formulas, the same four neighbor gathers, and a masked store at ptr_o + nc*PLANE + idx (per-lane offsets). Launch becomes grid=(cdiv(PLANE, BLOCK), N*C) with BLOCK chosen as a power of two in [32, 1024]. The exact-2x kernel, the wrapper selection logic and the public run() entrypoint are left unchanged.
record.expected: The 6 currently-failing formal cases compile and pass, so 24/24 correctness plus supplementary checks; timing-1 is expected to stay at the previously measured ~70 ms because the 2x fast path is deliberately untouched, so no target speedup is claimed by this call. Generic-path timing cases (timing-0/2/4) may shift in either direction.

alternatives: Keep the rank-2 kernel and only add a scalar-store special case for OH*OW==1 or OW==1: fixes that one shape but leaves the same degenerate splat-store form reachable for other foldings (e.g. OW==1 with a runtime length), so it is a narrower bet on the same unverified root cause.

Use tl.multiple_of/hint intrinsics to keep the pointer non-uniform without changing shapes: compiler folding of the weight/coordinate vectors would still collapse the offsets, and hints are IR-level anyway.
Run the generic path through the existing 2x-style kernel family for all ratios: wrong weights for non-2x scales, so not correctness-preserving.

record.discriminating_observation: The failed TTIR's store address operand is a splat of one scalar pointer (offset folded to `%c`), whereas the native IR that compiles has tt.addptr over a tensor<i64> of per-lane offsets with the same tensor<...x!tt.ptr<f16>> / tensor<...xf16> store signature. If the diagnosis holds, a rank-1 kernel that always stores through a per-lane index tensor will compile for exactly the shapes that previously failed.
